specification.problem: Given H=A+B with non-commuting A, B on a small register, find the Trotter number n minimizing the total variation distance between the output distribution of a noisy first-order Trotter circuit for exp(-iHt)|0..0> and the ideal exact distribution. Compare the numerically found n to the analytic n*=sqrt(a/(b*eps)).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: 2-qubit transverse-field Ising H=Z0Z1+g(X0+X1), initial state |00>, first-order Trotter, coherent over-rotation of size eps after each elementary gate (deterministic, statevector-friendly). Scan n and eps, find argmin of TV distance, compare to analytic n*. Out of scope: the paper's exact derivation and constants, stochastic or depolarizing noise averaging, Suzuki higher-order formulas (only the exponent change is noted), and any hardware calibration.

symbols.meaning: per-gate coherent over-rotation angle error strength
total variation distance between noisy Trotter and ideal computational-basis distributions
fitted coefficients of the Trotter error and the gate error

symbols.domain: positive real, rounded to an integer

equations.label: Trotter product with noisy gates
equations.description: First-order Trotter circuit in which each elementary gate has an extra coherent angle error eps. RX is applied to each of the two qubits. The gate count is about 3n.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes explicit over-rotation gates, and the abstract only says each gate is applied imperfectly.
assumptions: Qiskit RZZ(θ)=exp(-iθ ZZ/2) and RX(θ)=exp(-iθ X/2)

equations.label: Total variation distance
equations.description: Statistical distance between computational-basis distributions, computed classically from the statevector. The exact reference comes from matrix exponentiation.
equations.justification: The sketch fixes TV distance as the statistical distance. The abstract only mentions a statistical distance.
assumptions: The ideal reference is computed classically

equations.label: Error tradeoff model
equations.description: The first-order Trotter error falls as 1/n while the gate error grows linearly in the gate count. The squared-amplitude variant is a/n^2+b n^2 eps^2.
equations.abstract_quote: The resultant tradeoff in errors leads to an ultimate limit on the precision of the simulation.
equations.justification: The abstract states the tradeoff qualitatively. The 1/n and n*eps forms are the standard leading-order scalings from the sketch, not the paper's confirmed result.
assumptions: Coefficients a and b fitted numerically or estimated

equations.label: Optimal Trotter number
equations.description: Minimizer of eq_3, obtained by setting dD/dn=0. It gives n* proportional to eps^(-1/2) and D_min proportional to eps^(1/2).
equations.abstract_quote: We calculate the optimum Trotter number $n^{*}$ that achieves this limit
equations.justification: The abstract says an optimum n* is computed. This closed form follows from the assumed eq_3 model.

equations.label: Higher-order scaling
equations.description: For a p-th order product formula the optimal n shifts to this exponent.
equations.justification: Follows from minimizing the assumed model. Out of scope for the circuit.
assumptions: Gate count per step is held fixed in the scaling

registers.name: sys
registers.role: system qubits, little-endian, qubit 0 is the least significant bit of the outcome index

specification.initial_state: |00> (all qubits in the ground computational state)

steps.description: Build H=Z0Z1+g(X0+X1) with e.g. g=1 and t=1. Compute the exact distribution classically by matrix exponentiation of the 4x4 H.
For each n in a range (e.g. 1..200) and each eps, build the circuit: n repetitions of RZZ(2t/n+eps) on (0,1), then RX(2gt/n+eps) on qubit 0 and on qubit 1. No measurements; read the statevector.
Compute D(n) from the statevector probabilities and the exact distribution. Find the integer n minimizing D.
Fit a and b from the small-n regime (eps=0 gives a) and the large-n regime. Compare the numerical argmin with n* and check the scaling in eps and t.

specification.measurement: No hardware measurement. The simulator reads the statevector, and probabilities |amplitude|^2 are indexed in little-endian order (qubit 0 is the last character of a bit string).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute the exact reference distribution, TV distance for each n, the argmin over n, the fitted a and b, the analytic n*, and log-log slopes of n* versus eps (expect -1/2 for first order).
assumptions: The target instance (2-qubit TFIM, g=1, t=1) was chosen by me, not given in the abstract
Coherent noise is used in place of stochastic noise so the statevector run is deterministic
With coherent noise, errors may add or cancel with the Trotter error, so D(n) may be non-monotone; use a sign-fixed eps
No ancilla needed since the readout is computational-basis probabilities
missing_information: Paper's actual noise model and definition of statistical distance
Paper's exact formulas and constants for n*
Whether the paper treats Hamiltonians with many terms or a specific system
